full.description: This is a photomicrograph of a blood vessel, specifically a saphenous vein graft showing sclerotic changes. The cross-section highlights intimal thickening and fibrosis characteristic of vein graft atherosclerosis or sclerosis. Special staining reveals the structural components of the vessel wall, such as collagen and elastic fibers. The image demonstrates marked luminal narrowing and remodeling typical of advanced graft disease.

blind.description: This is a micrograph of brain tissue showing areas of early myelin loss accompanied by enlarged oligodendrocyte nuclei. The oligodendrocyte nuclei are positively stained for viral antigens surrounding the demyelinating lesions. These findings are characteristic of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, a viral demyelinating disease of the central nervous system.

random.description: This is a photomicrograph of splenic tissue, characteristic of an old spleen infarct stained to highlight specific structures such as connective tissue and reticulin fibers. The image demonstrates a well-demarcated region of ischemic necrosis and fibrous replacement. The pale, acellular area represents the infarcted parenchyma surrounded by a capsule or border of fibrous connective tissue. Such findings are typical of healed splenic infarction resulting from vascular occlusion.
